key_insight: The paper shows that using a log-barrier regularizer plus a dual-focused analysis yields the first algorithm that attains the optimal last-iterate convergence rate for uncoupled zero-sum matrix games with bandit feedback, matching the known lower bound of order t^{-1/4}.
problem_solved: How to learn minimax policies (last-iterate convergence) in zero-sum matrix games when players receive only bandit (partial) feedback and act uncoupled—previous methods failed to reach the provable optimal rate.
method: Introduce a log-barrier regularization inside an online mirror-descent style algorithm to stabilize iterates near the simplex boundary.
Develop a dual-focused analysis tailored to the log-barrier geometry to control the exploitability of the actual (last) iterate rather than averages.
Handle bandit feedback with appropriate gradient/importance-weighted estimators and variance control to preserve the t^{-1/4} rate under partial information.
impact: Provides the first practical/theoretical recipe to guarantee optimal last-iterate convergence under realistic partial-feedback conditions, improving stability and sample-efficiency for learning minimax strategies in adversarial settings.
visual_elements: Two-player zero-sum payoff matrix icon with arrows depicting uncoupled players and bandit (partial) feedback
Convergence chart comparing last-iterate vs. averaged-iterate rates, highlighting the t^{-1/4} slope and matching the lower bound
Algorithm flow: (1) sample/bandit observation → (2) importance-weighted gradient estimate → (3) log-barrier mirror-descent update
Illustration of simplex with log-barrier preventing boundary collapse (iterates staying interior)
paper_title: Optimal last-iterate convergence in matrix games with bandit feedback using the log-barrier
paper_authors: Come Fiegel, Pierre Menard, Tadashi Kozuno, Michal Valko, Vianney Perchet
